classification.difficultyReason: Development: link four explicit clues to the five displayed heights, beginning with the tallest column, then applying the half and one-fewer relationships and ordering the two remaining categories. The deduction is multistep but has a clear supplied starting point.

inlines.text: Use these clues to work out the labels on the
The number of people who own a cat is half of the number of people who own a dog.
More people own a dog than any other animal.
More people own a horse than a rabbit.
One fewer person owns a hamster than a cat.

answer.short:
Left to right: Hamster, Rabbit, Cat, Dog, Horse.

Label the tallest column Dog, then use the clues to match the remaining heights.
answer.worked:
Dog has the tallest column, so $8$ people own a dog.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Cat owners}&=8\div2\\&=4\\\text{Hamster owners}&=4-1\\&=3\end{align*}$$
The remaining heights are $6$ and $7$. More people own a horse than a rabbit, so horse is $7$ and rabbit is $6$.

Left to right: Hamster, Rabbit, Cat, Dog, Horse.
